questions.question: If a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) but the tractor does not:

options.text: You cannot drive the truck because ABS must be on both the tractor and trailer.
You must drive slower than normal.
You must get a different tractor that has ABS.
You can still use the tractor and trailer together.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still use the tractor and trailer together.
questions.explanation: Having anti-lock brakes on just the tractor or just the trailer gives you better control when braking.

questions.question: How often must workers who handle hazardous materials be trained?

options.text: At least once every three years

questions.correctAnswerText: At least once every three years
questions.explanation: Workers who handle hazardous materials must be trained and tested at least once every three years.

questions.question: You may be an aggressive driver if you:

options.text: Plan ahead for delays on your drive.
Keep a safe distance between you and other vehicles.
Make rude hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make rude hand gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan for extra travel time, allow for delays, keep a safe following distance, and never make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Is not available on most trucks.
Does not help in most situations.

questions.explanation: Starting between 1997 and 1999, most commercial vehicles, trailers, and dollies must have ABS.

questions.question: When you plan to change lanes, you should check your mirrors:

options.text: The same as you normally do.
More often than you normally do.

questions.correctAnswerText: More often than you normally do.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly as part of normal driving. When changing lanes, check your mirrors even more carefully.

questions.question: When carrying packages with radioactive materials, you should know that:

options.text: Radiation can pass through to other packages.
The packages must be carried in the cab.
The packages must be laid on their side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation can pass through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from radioactive packages to nearby packages. Because of this, there are limits on how many radioactive packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: The service air line connects to the:
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air that you control with the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: An air supply control lever should be in the "normal" position when you are:
questions.explanation: Older tractors may have levers instead of knobs to control air supply. When the air supply control is in the "normal" position, it is correctly set for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: When driving:

options.text: Do not let other drivers know what you plan to do.
Only use turn signals if other vehicles are nearby.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Communicate with other drivers on the road. Always signal before you turn or change lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: By placing it in a certain part of the trailer.

questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label does not fit on a package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: What affects stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, its weight, and how slippery the road is.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, when should you shift into a lower gear?

options.text: As you go downhill and pick up speed.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. Shifting down at high speeds can damage the transmission and reduce your ability to engine brake. Choose a safe speed based on the hill's steepness and length, your vehicle's weight, and road and weather conditions.

questions.question: Which is not an exhaust system problem?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are not leaking

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not leaking
questions.explanation: When checking the exhaust system, make sure all parts are tight, not broken, and not missing. Parts must be properly mounted and not rubbing against other vehicle parts.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before your trip. Make sure the trailer rolls freely, then pull out the trailer air supply control to the emergency position. Pull forward slightly and check that the trailer does not move.

questions.question: When visibility is low at dawn or dusk, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When driving at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to improve visibility.

questions.question: What does Gross Combination Weight mean?

options.text: The total weight of the powered unit, trailer, and cargo
The total weight of a single vehicle without its load
The maximum weight allowed by the manufacturer

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the powered unit, trailer, and cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Combination Weight (GCW) is the total weight of the powered unit, trailer, and cargo together.

questions.question: When braking, your vehicle should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, there may be a brake problem.

questions.question: What happens if brakes overheat going downhill?
questions.explanation: Overusing the brakes makes them overheat and less effective. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: How must a hazardous waste manifest be signed?

options.text: On the outside of the trailer.

questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. The manifest must be signed by hand.
